questions.question: Which storage service can be used as a low-cost option for hosting static websites?

explanation.summary: Amazon Glacier is designed for archival storage and is not optimized for hosting websites due to high retrieval latency.
explanation.why: While Glacier offers very low-cost storage, it is intended for long-term archival and infrequently accessed data. Hosting a static website requires low-latency retrieval and availability, which Glacier does not provide.

explanation.summary: DynamoDB is a NoSQL database service and not suitable for static website hosting.
explanation.why: DynamoDB stores data in tables for dynamic access, not for serving static web content like HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.

explanation.summary: Amazon EFS is a scalable file storage for Linux workloads and is not a cost-efficient static website hosting solution.
explanation.why: EFS is designed for shared file storage and high throughput, but its pricing and access patterns are not optimized for hosting static websites.

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 is a highly durable object storage service that can host static websites at low cost.
keyPoints: Provides simple web hosting for static content
Low-cost storage options with pay-as-you-go pricing
Can integrate with CloudFront for CDN distribution
Simple management and scalability without server maintenance
Supports routing rules and custom domain names
examples: Host HTML/CSS/JS website directly from an S3 bucket
Use CloudFront with S3 for global low-latency access
explanation.additionalInfo: S3 static website hosting allows you to serve content without provisioning servers, supports index and error documents, and integrates seamlessly with Route 53 for custom domains. Cost scales with storage and data transfer, making it a very economical solution for static sites.

learnMore.title: Host a Static Website on Amazon S3

questions.question: Which Amazon EC2 instance pricing model can provide discounts of up to 90%?

explanation.summary: Reserved Instances provide predictable discounts but not up to 90%.
explanation.why: Reserved Instances require a commitment period (1–3 years) and typically offer up to 72% savings compared to On-Demand, not the maximum 90% offered by Spot Instances.

explanation.summary: On-Demand pricing has no upfront commitment and no discounts of this magnitude.
explanation.why: On-Demand instances are billed at standard rates, providing flexibility but not large discounts.

explanation.summary: Dedicated Hosts are physical servers dedicated to your account and do not offer up to 90% discounts.
explanation.why: Dedicated Hosts provide control over instance placement but are billed at higher rates; large discounts are not applied as with Spot Instances.

explanation.summary: Spot Instances allow you to use spare EC2 capacity at steep discounts, often up to 90% off On-Demand pricing.
keyPoints: Significant cost savings compared to On-Demand
Used for batch processing, big data, CI/CD jobs
Fully integrated with AWS pricing and APIs
Requires workloads that can tolerate interruptions
examples: Run a large batch job using Spot Instances to reduce cost
Use Spot Instances for scalable data processing pipelines
explanation.additionalInfo: Spot Instances are suitable for workloads that are stateless, flexible, or can checkpoint progress. They offer the highest savings among EC2 pricing models and integrate with Auto Scaling to optimize costs.

questions.question: What is the AWS customer responsible for according to the AWS shared responsibility model?

explanation.summary: Physical access to AWS data centers is managed entirely by AWS.
explanation.why: Customers never have physical access to AWS infrastructure; AWS ensures physical security.

explanation.summary: Customers are responsible for encrypting their data at rest and in transit.
keyPoints: Encrypt sensitive data stored in AWS services
Manage encryption keys using AWS KMS or customer-managed keys
Ensure secure transmission of data to and from AWS
Comply with regulatory requirements for data protection
Apply encryption to application-level data if necessary
examples: Encrypt S3 bucket data using server-side encryption
Use TLS for data sent to an EC2-hosted web application
explanation.additionalInfo: While AWS manages the security of the cloud infrastructure, customers must manage data security, including encryption, access controls, and application security.

learnMore.title: AWS Shared Responsibility Model - Data Security

explanation.summary: AWS is responsible for securely disposing of physical storage media.
explanation.why: Customers do not handle AWS physical devices; AWS ensures proper disposal.

explanation.summary: AWS manages environmental risks in its data centers.
explanation.why: Customers are not responsible for facility environmental controls; AWS handles power, cooling, and disaster mitigation.

questions.question: Which of the following AWS Cloud services can be used to run a customer-managed relational database?

explanation.summary: Amazon EC2 allows customers to run relational databases on virtual servers they manage.
keyPoints: Full control over database software and configuration
Customer is responsible for OS, backups, patching, and scaling
Can install MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, etc.
Ideal for custom database requirements or legacy applications
Supports HA and replication through customer-managed configurations
Pay-as-you-go pricing based on instance usage
Integration with other AWS services for networking and storage
examples: Running a MySQL database on an EC2 instance for a legacy application
Deploying a custom PostgreSQL cluster with specific extensions on EC2
explanation.additionalInfo: Using EC2 for a managed relational database requires customers to handle maintenance tasks manually, unlike RDS. This provides flexibility at the cost of operational overhead.

explanation.summary: Route 53 is a DNS service and does not host databases.
explanation.why: It provides domain name resolution and routing but cannot run relational databases.

explanation.summary: ElastiCache is an in-memory caching service and not a relational database service.
explanation.why: ElastiCache provides Redis or Memcached caching layers, not persistent relational data storage.

explanation.summary: DynamoDB is a managed NoSQL database and does not allow customer-managed relational databases.
explanation.why: It is schema-less and optimized for key-value/document workloads, not relational databases managed by customers.

questions.question: A company is looking for a scalable data warehouse solution. Which of the following AWS solutions would meet the company’s needs?

explanation.summary: S3 is object storage, not a data warehouse.
explanation.why: While S3 can store large amounts of data, it does not provide analytical query engines or structured data warehouse capabilities.

explanation.summary: DynamoDB is a NoSQL database, not a data warehouse.
explanation.why: It supports key-value/document workloads but lacks the SQL-based analytics and data warehousing capabilities.

explanation.summary: Kinesis is a streaming data service and not a data warehouse.
explanation.why: It is designed for real-time data streaming and analytics, not for storing structured warehouse data for complex queries.

explanation.summary: Amazon Redshift is a fully managed, petabyte-scale data warehouse service.
keyPoints: Integrates with BI tools and SQL clients
Can query data directly from S3 with Redshift Spectrum
examples: Analyze sales data across multiple years using Redshift
Use Redshift for scalable reporting and analytics from operational databases
explanation.additionalInfo: Redshift provides a high-performance, fully managed data warehouse optimized for OLAP workloads. It integrates with AWS ecosystem services and third-party analytics tools, enabling scalable, fast querying of structured and semi-structured datasets.

questions.question: Which statement best describes Elastic Load Balancing?

options.text: It translates a domain name into an IP address using DNS.

explanation.summary: DNS translation is not the function of Elastic Load Balancing.
explanation.why: Route 53 or standard DNS services perform domain-to-IP translation, while ELB distributes traffic across instances.

options.text: It distributes incoming application traffic across one or more Amazon EC2 instances.

explanation.summary: Elastic Load Balancing automatically distributes incoming application traffic across multiple targets for high availability.
keyPoints: Supports Application Load Balancer (ALB), Network Load Balancer (NLB), and Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB)
Improves fault tolerance by distributing traffic
Can scale automatically to handle varying traffic
Supports health checks to route traffic only to healthy instances
Integrates with Auto Scaling for elasticity
Allows secure access through TLS termination
examples: Distribute HTTP requests among multiple web servers
Route TCP traffic across several EC2 backend instances
explanation.additionalInfo: ELB ensures applications remain available and responsive by balancing loads across EC2 instances or other resources. It supports high availability, automatic scaling, and secure traffic management.

options.text: It collects metrics on connected Amazon EC2 instances.

explanation.summary: Metrics collection is handled by Amazon CloudWatch, not ELB.
explanation.why: ELB distributes traffic; CloudWatch monitors instance and load balancer metrics.

options.text: It automatically adjusts the number of Amazon EC2 instances to support incoming traffic.

explanation.summary: Auto Scaling adjusts instance counts, not ELB.
explanation.why: While ELB works with Auto Scaling, it itself does not change instance numbers.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid ways for a customer to interact with AWS services? (Select TWO.)

explanation.summary: AWS CLI allows programmatic access to AWS services from a terminal or script.
keyPoints: Access AWS services without console UI
Provides access to all service APIs
examples: Use CLI to create S3 buckets or EC2 instances
Automate deployment scripts using CLI commands
explanation.additionalInfo: The AWS CLI is widely used for automation, scripting, and managing AWS resources programmatically, offering the same functionality as the console with better reproducibility.

explanation.summary: Being on-premises is not a method to interact with AWS services directly.
explanation.why: Physical on-premises locations cannot directly access AWS services without network connectivity; it is not a valid interaction method.

explanation.summary: AWS SDKs allow applications in various programming languages to interact with AWS services.
keyPoints: Available for multiple languages (Python, Java, .NET, JavaScript, etc.)
Supports features like signing requests and error handling
examples: Use Boto3 SDK in Python to interact with S3 or DynamoDB
Java SDK for provisioning EC2 instances programmatically
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS SDKs abstract raw API calls, providing idiomatic interfaces in each language, enabling developers to integrate AWS service calls directly into their applications efficiently.

explanation.summary: SaaS refers to cloud applications and is not a method for customers to interact with AWS infrastructure services.
explanation.why: SaaS consumes AWS resources indirectly but is not a direct access method for interacting with AWS services.

explanation.summary: Hybrid architecture combines on-premises and cloud infrastructure but is not itself a direct method of interaction.
explanation.why: Being hybrid describes deployment topology, not a way to interact programmatically with AWS services.

questions.question: The AWS Cloud’s multiple Regions are an example of:

explanation.summary: Agility refers to quickly provisioning resources, not the geographical spread.
explanation.why: While agility is a cloud benefit, multiple Regions specifically demonstrate AWS’s global infrastructure, not resource speed.

explanation.summary: Multiple Regions worldwide exemplify AWS global infrastructure.
keyPoints: Availability Zones within regions provide fault isolation
Reduces latency by serving users nearby
Supports compliance with data residency requirements
Forms the backbone for cloud scalability and high availability
examples: Deploy a web app to US-East-1, EU-West-1 for global users
Use multiple Regions for disaster recovery scenarios
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS operates 33+ Regions worldwide, each with multiple Availability Zones. This setup allows customers to build highly available, resilient, and low-latency applications globally.

explanation.summary: Elasticity is the ability to scale resources up/down based on demand, not geographic spread.
explanation.why: Regions do not represent dynamic scaling; they provide physical infrastructure locations.

explanation.summary: Pay-as-you-go refers to billing based on consumption, unrelated to multiple Regions.
explanation.why: Regions describe physical infrastructure, not pricing models.

questions.question: Which of the following AWS services can be used to serve large amounts of online video content with the lowest possible latency? (Select TWO.)

explanation.summary: Storage Gateway provides hybrid cloud storage, not content delivery.
explanation.why: It facilitates on-premises access to cloud storage, but does not optimize global video delivery or low-latency streaming.

explanation.summary: S3 stores video content reliably and scales to large volumes.
keyPoints: Can host video files for streaming
Works with CloudFront for global delivery
Supports scalable storage without upfront provisioning
examples: Store and serve VOD content from S3 buckets
Use S3 as origin for CloudFront CDN
explanation.additionalInfo: S3 provides scalable storage for large media files. While latency is improved with CloudFront, S3 serves as the origin for global content distribution.

learnMore.title: Deliver content faster with CloudFront and S3

explanation.summary: EFS is a shared file system for Linux workloads, not optimized for high-performance video delivery.
explanation.why: EFS provides file-level storage over NFS and is not a global low-latency content distribution service.

explanation.summary: Glacier is for archival storage, not for low-latency content delivery.
explanation.why: Retrieval from Glacier can take minutes to hours, unsuitable for video streaming.

explanation.summary: CloudFront is a CDN that delivers content globally with low latency.
keyPoints: Distributes content to edge locations worldwide
Reduces latency by serving content closer to users
Integrates with S3 as an origin
Enables scalable delivery of video, images, and static content
Works with signed URLs and geo-restriction
Provides real-time metrics for content usage
examples: Stream video to users across multiple continents with minimal buffering
Serve large media files globally with high performance
explanation.additionalInfo: CloudFront leverages a network of edge locations to optimize content delivery. Combining S3 as the origin and CloudFront as CDN enables scalable, low-latency streaming for video applications.

questions.question: Web servers running on Amazon EC2 access a legacy application running in a corporate data center. What term would describe this model?

explanation.summary: Cloud-native refers to applications fully designed to run in the cloud, not integrated with on-premises systems.
explanation.why: Since the legacy application resides on-premises and EC2 servers connect to it, this architecture is not cloud-native.

explanation.summary: A partner network refers to AWS Partner Programs, not hybrid deployment models.
explanation.why: The question describes system architecture, not partnerships.

explanation.summary: Hybrid architecture combines cloud and on-premises resources to work together.
keyPoints: Integrates on-premises applications with cloud workloads
Enables low-latency access to legacy systems
Allows cloud scalability while leveraging existing infrastructure
Supports hybrid networking like VPN or Direct Connect
Useful for legacy integration and phased modernization
examples: EC2 web servers accessing on-premises Oracle database
Hybrid cloud backup solutions with Storage Gateway
explanation.additionalInfo: Hybrid architecture is common when organizations cannot fully migrate legacy applications to the cloud but want to leverage AWS services for new workloads or elasticity.

explanation.summary: IaaS refers to cloud service model providing compute, storage, and networking, not a hybrid deployment pattern.
explanation.why: The model described combines on-premises and cloud systems; IaaS alone does not describe this hybrid topology.

questions.question: What is the benefit of using AWS managed services, such as Amazon ElastiCache and Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS)?

options.text: They require the customer to monitor and replace failing instances.

explanation.summary: AWS managed services handle monitoring and instance replacement automatically.
explanation.why: Customers are relieved from manually handling hardware or OS failures; AWS performs these tasks.

options.text: They have better performance than customer-managed services.

explanation.summary: Performance depends on configuration and workload; managed services do not automatically guarantee higher performance.
explanation.why: AWS managed services simplify operations but performance is still workload-dependent and requires tuning.

options.text: They simplify patching and updating underlying OSs.

explanation.summary: AWS managed services handle operating system patching and updates, reducing operational burden.
keyPoints: Automated patching for OS and database software
Regular maintenance windows managed by AWS
Customers focus on applications, not infrastructure
Reduces downtime risk from manual patching
examples: RDS automatically applies OS security patches during maintenance
ElastiCache nodes are patched without customer intervention
explanation.additionalInfo: Managed services offload operational tasks such as OS maintenance, backups, and patching, allowing customers to focus on application logic and business value.

options.text: They do not require the customer to optimize instance type or size selections.

explanation.summary: Customers still choose instance types and sizes based on workload requirements.
explanation.why: AWS simplifies OS and software management, but capacity planning and instance selection remain customer responsibilities.

questions.question: Which service provides a virtually unlimited amount of online highly durable object storage?

explanation.summary: Redshift is a data warehouse, not object storage.
explanation.why: While Redshift stores structured data for analytics, it does not provide object storage with virtually unlimited capacity.

explanation.summary: EFS provides scalable file storage for Linux workloads, not object storage.
explanation.why: EFS is a file system with POSIX interface; it is not designed for virtually unlimited object storage with high durability.

explanation.summary: ECS is a container orchestration service, not object storage.
explanation.why: ECS runs containers but does not provide durable storage for objects.

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 provides virtually unlimited, highly durable object storage in the cloud.
keyPoints: Stores objects with unique keys in buckets
examples: Store backups, media files, and large datasets in S3
Use S3 as origin for CloudFront distribution
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon S3 is a foundational AWS service for storing any amount of data with high durability and availability. It supports object tagging, encryption, access policies, and lifecycle management, making it suitable for backup, archival, and content delivery.

questions.question: Which of the following Identity and Access Management (IAM) entities is associated with an access key ID and secret access key when using AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI)?

explanation.summary: IAM groups are collections of users for policy management and do not have access keys.
explanation.why: Access keys are tied to individual users or root accounts, not groups.

explanation.summary: IAM users have long-term credentials, including access key ID and secret access key, for programmatic access.
keyPoints: Associated with a single person or application
Used for CLI, SDK, and API access
Can be assigned policies for fine-grained permissions
Credentials include password for console and access keys for programmatic access
Enables audit and accountability for actions
Access keys can be rotated regularly for security
examples: A developer uses AWS CLI with their IAM user's access keys to deploy S3 buckets
Service account IAM user accesses DynamoDB programmatically
explanation.additionalInfo: Access keys allow programmatic authentication to AWS without using the web console. IAM users provide controlled, auditable access and can be managed individually or via groups.

explanation.summary: IAM roles are assumed by entities and provide temporary credentials, not permanent access keys tied directly to the role.
explanation.why: Roles do not have fixed access key IDs and secret access keys; they issue temporary credentials when assumed.

explanation.summary: IAM policies define permissions and do not have credentials themselves.
explanation.why: Policies cannot be used to log in or authenticate; they attach to users, groups, or roles.

questions.question: Which of the following security-related services does AWS offer? (Select TWO.)

explanation.summary: AWS supports MFA, but physical tokens are an implementation choice, not a managed service.
explanation.why: AWS provides MFA via virtual and hardware devices, but the MFA tokens themselves are not a standalone AWS service.

explanation.summary: Trusted Advisor provides security checks to help optimize and secure AWS resources.
keyPoints: Helps identify overly permissive IAM roles
Highlights exposed access keys and unencrypted resources
examples: Trusted Advisor alerting about S3 buckets with public access
Recommendations to rotate IAM access keys
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Trusted Advisor helps customers ensure their AWS environment adheres to best practices for security, cost optimization, and fault tolerance.

explanation.summary: AWS offers encryption features across services for data at rest and in transit.
keyPoints: Server-side encryption for S3, RDS, EBS
AWS Key Management Service (KMS) for key management
Encryption integrated into services like DynamoDB and EFS
Can encrypt backups and snapshots automatically
examples: Encrypt S3 bucket objects using SSE-KMS
Enable encryption for RDS database instances
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS provides robust encryption capabilities to secure data both at rest and in transit. Customers can manage keys via KMS or use service-managed keys.

explanation.summary: AWS does not offer automated penetration testing as a service; customers perform penetration tests.
explanation.why: AWS provides guidance for penetration testing but does not automate the process as a service.

explanation.summary: S3 itself does not provide content copyright detection as a managed service.
explanation.why: Customers must implement their own detection or use third-party tools; AWS S3 is storage only.

questions.question: Which AWS managed service is used to host databases?

explanation.summary: AWS Batch is for running batch computing workloads, not hosting databases.
explanation.why: It manages containerized batch jobs on EC2 or Fargate but does not provide database hosting.

explanation.summary: AWS Artifact provides compliance and security reports, not database hosting.
explanation.why: It is a compliance portal, unrelated to database services.

explanation.summary: Data Pipeline orchestrates data workflows but does not host databases.
explanation.why: It moves and transforms data between storage and compute services but is not a database service.

explanation.summary: Amazon RDS is a managed relational database service that handles provisioning, patching, and backups.
keyPoints: Supports multiple database engines (MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, Aurora)
Automates hardware provisioning, OS patching, and backups
Enables scaling of compute and storage
Reduces operational overhead compared to self-managed databases
Secure integration with VPC, IAM, and KMS
Ideal for OLTP and production workloads
examples: Host a production MySQL database with automated backups
Deploy PostgreSQL for web application backend without managing servers
explanation.additionalInfo: RDS simplifies relational database management, letting customers focus on applications rather than underlying infrastructure. It provides automated failover, backup, and scaling options.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides a simple and scalable shared file storage solution for use with Linux-based AWS and on-premises servers?

explanation.summary: S3 is object storage, not a shared file system.
explanation.why: While S3 stores objects, it does not provide a POSIX-compliant file system interface suitable for Linux workloads needing shared access.

explanation.summary: Glacier is archival storage, not a shared file system.
explanation.why: It is optimized for long-term storage and does not provide real-time file system access for Linux servers.

explanation.summary: EBS provides block storage for single EC2 instances, not shared file storage.
explanation.why: EBS volumes attach to a single instance at a time and are not suitable for shared file access across multiple servers.

explanation.summary: Amazon EFS provides a scalable, managed NFS file system for Linux workloads accessible from AWS and on-premises servers.
keyPoints: Supports multiple EC2 instances and on-premises servers
Scales automatically as data grows or shrinks
Supports throughput and IOPS scaling for variable workloads
Integrates with AWS security and networking
Ideal for content management, web serving, and analytics workloads
examples: Shared home directories for Linux web servers
High-performance file storage for application workloads requiring multiple access points
explanation.additionalInfo: EFS eliminates the need to provision or manage storage capacity manually. It is designed for high availability and durability across multiple Availability Zones.

questions.question: When architecting cloud applications, which of the following are key design principles?

explanation.summary: Using the largest instance is not a recommended design principle; elasticity is preferred.
explanation.why: Provisioning for peaks is inefficient; cloud best practices emphasize scaling resources dynamically.

explanation.summary: Provisioning for peak load is traditional IT thinking; cloud best practices rely on elasticity.
explanation.why: Cloud resources can scale up or down, so over-provisioning for peaks is inefficient.

explanation.summary: Scrum is a software development methodology, not a cloud architecture principle.
explanation.why: While Scrum can be used in cloud projects, it is not a design principle for cloud applications.

explanation.summary: Elasticity allows cloud applications to scale resources up or down based on demand.
keyPoints: Optimize costs by using resources only when needed
Supports fault tolerance and high availability
Enables responsive performance during traffic spikes
Integrates with Auto Scaling and managed services
examples: Auto Scaling EC2 instances based on CPU utilization
Automatically expanding S3 storage or EFS file system
explanation.additionalInfo: Elasticity is a fundamental principle in cloud architecture to ensure efficient resource use, cost optimization, and responsiveness to changing workloads.

questions.question: Which AWS service should be used for long-term, low-cost storage of data backups?

explanation.summary: RDS is a managed relational database service, not primarily a long-term low-cost storage solution.
explanation.why: While RDS handles database snapshots and backups, it is not optimized for long-term archival storage.

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 Glacier is a secure, durable, low-cost storage service for long-term data archiving and backups.
keyPoints: Designed for archival and infrequently accessed data
Extremely low storage cost per GB
Integrates with S3 for lifecycle policies
Supports compliance and regulatory retention requirements
Data retrieval options with varying latency (minutes to hours)
Ideal for backups, archives, and long-term retention
examples: Store regulatory backups for 7+ years
Archive historical application logs
explanation.additionalInfo: Glacier provides a cost-effective solution for organizations needing durable storage for archival and backup purposes, with retrieval times configurable based on urgency.

explanation.summary: Snowball is a data transfer service, not long-term storage.
explanation.why: Snowball moves large amounts of data to AWS but does not provide ongoing storage; data is ultimately stored in S3 or Glacier.

explanation.summary: EBS provides block storage for EC2, not long-term archival storage.
explanation.why: EBS is intended for live application storage with higher cost; it is not optimized for low-cost archival backups.

questions.question: Which task is AWS responsible for in the shared responsibility model for security and compliance?

options.text: Granting access to individuals and services

explanation.summary: Granting access is a customer responsibility.
explanation.why: Customers manage IAM users, roles, and permissions to control who can access AWS resources.

explanation.summary: AWS provides infrastructure and network protections to encrypt data in transit.
keyPoints: Automated encryption between AWS data centers
Part of AWS’s responsibility for security of the cloud
examples: Automatic HTTPS enforcement for S3 and CloudFront
Encryption of traffic between Availability Zones
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS manages security of the underlying cloud infrastructure, including encryption in transit, while customers are responsible for managing data security within their accounts.

explanation.summary: AWS manages host firmware updates.
explanation.why: Customers do not control the underlying EC2 hardware; AWS applies updates as part of managed infrastructure.

explanation.summary: OS patching for managed services like RDS is handled by AWS; for EC2 instances, customers manage the OS.
explanation.why: Responsibility varies by service; customers control OS updates for self-managed instances.

questions.question: Where should a company go to search software listings from independent software vendors to find, test, buy and deploy software that runs on AWS?

explanation.summary: AWS Marketplace is a digital catalog for software from independent vendors to deploy on AWS.
keyPoints: Provides pre-configured software for AWS deployment
Includes security, compliance, and licensing information
Enables easy testing, purchasing, and deployment
examples: Deploying a database solution from AWS Marketplace
Using a monitoring tool AMI directly in your VPC
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Marketplace simplifies finding and deploying third-party software on AWS, ensuring compatibility and billing integration.

explanation.summary: Lumberyard is a game engine, not a software marketplace.
explanation.why: It provides development tools for games, unrelated to deploying third-party software on AWS.

explanation.summary: AWS Artifact provides compliance reports, not software deployment.
explanation.why: It is a central repository for security and compliance documentation, not for sourcing software.

explanation.summary: CloudSearch is a managed search service, not a software marketplace.
explanation.why: It provides search functionality for applications, unrelated to deploying third-party software.

questions.question: Which of the following is a benefit of using the AWS Cloud?

options.text: Permissive security removes the administrative burden.

explanation.summary: AWS does not remove the need for customers to manage security responsibly.
explanation.why: Security is shared; customers must implement access controls, policies, and encryption.

options.text: Ability to focus on revenue-generating activities.

explanation.summary: AWS reduces operational overhead, allowing businesses to focus on core revenue activities.
keyPoints: Reduces time spent on maintenance and patching
Frees staff to focus on business value
examples: Startups deploying apps quickly without managing servers
Enterprises shifting focus from data center operations to application features
explanation.additionalInfo: By using AWS managed services and scalable infrastructure, organizations can allocate resources to strategic initiatives rather than maintaining hardware or repetitive operational tasks.

learnMore.title: IDC Report on AWS Cloud Benefits

explanation.summary: AWS customers do not control physical cloud network hardware.
explanation.why: AWS manages all underlying infrastructure; customers manage resources at the software level.

options.text: Choice of specific cloud hardware vendors.

explanation.summary: AWS abstracts hardware vendor choices from customers.
explanation.why: Customers consume AWS services without selecting underlying hardware vendors.

questions.question: When performing a cost analysis that supports physical isolation of a customer workload, which compute hosting model should be accounted for in the Total Cost of Ownership (TCO)?

explanation.summary: Dedicated Hosts are physical servers dedicated to a single customer, suitable for TCO calculations for isolated workloads.
keyPoints: Provides physical isolation for compliance and licensing
Allows use of existing server-bound software licenses
Gives visibility into instance placement on the host
Helps meet regulatory and audit requirements
Billed per physical server instead of per instance
examples: Deploy Windows Server workloads with BYOL licenses on Dedicated Hosts
Calculate cost for workloads that must run on isolated physical infrastructure
explanation.additionalInfo: Dedicated Hosts are important for scenarios requiring physical isolation for licensing, compliance, or security. TCO calculations must include the cost of dedicated server usage compared to shared or virtualized hosting.

explanation.summary: Reserved Instances provide discounted pricing for committed instance usage but do not guarantee physical isolation.
explanation.why: RI are virtualized and may share physical hardware with other customers; TCO for isolated workloads requires Dedicated Hosts.

explanation.summary: On-Demand Instances provide flexibility but run on shared hardware.
explanation.why: They do not provide guaranteed physical isolation, so TCO for isolated workloads is not based on On-Demand pricing.

explanation.summary: No Upfront RIs are a payment option and do not provide physical isolation.
explanation.why: They are a pricing choice for virtualized instances; isolation is not guaranteed.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides the ability to manage infrastructure as code?

explanation.summary: CodePipeline orchestrates CI/CD pipelines but does not define infrastructure as code.
explanation.why: It automates build and deployment workflows but does not provision resources declaratively.

explanation.summary: CodeDeploy handles deployment to instances but does not manage infrastructure as code.
explanation.why: It deploys applications, but provisioning of underlying infrastructure is outside its scope.

explanation.summary: Direct Connect provides dedicated network connections and is not infrastructure as code.
explanation.why: It establishes private connectivity but does not define cloud resources declaratively.

explanation.summary: CloudFormation allows provisioning and managing AWS resources using templates as code.
keyPoints: Define resources declaratively in JSON or YAML templates
Automate deployment of EC2, S3, RDS, and other resources
Supports version control and repeatable deployments
Enables infrastructure as code for dev, test, and production
examples: Create an entire VPC with EC2, RDS, and S3 buckets via a CloudFormation template
Deploy multi-tier application stacks consistently across regions
explanation.additionalInfo: CloudFormation provides full infrastructure automation, enabling reproducible deployments and codified environments.

questions.question: If a customer needs to audit the change management of AWS resources, which of the following AWS services should the customer use?

explanation.summary: AWS Config monitors and records configuration changes to AWS resources for auditing and compliance.
keyPoints: Supports compliance audits and operational analysis
Automates evaluation of configurations against policies
Integrates with CloudTrail for activity logs
examples: Detect changes to security groups over time
Audit S3 bucket policy modifications for compliance
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Config is designed to help customers maintain compliance, troubleshoot operational issues, and manage resource changes efficiently.

explanation.summary: Trusted Advisor provides best-practice checks, not detailed change auditing.
explanation.why: It identifies potential security, cost, and performance improvements but does not track resource configuration changes over time.

explanation.summary: CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs but does not provide change management auditing.
explanation.why: CloudWatch tracks performance and operational metrics; it does not audit resource configuration changes.

explanation.summary: Inspector performs security assessments, not auditing of configuration changes.
explanation.why: It analyzes security posture and vulnerabilities, but does not track historical resource configurations.

questions.question: What is Amazon CloudWatch?

options.text: A code repository with customizable build and team commit features.

explanation.summary: CloudWatch is not a code repository; it is a monitoring service.
explanation.why: AWS CodeCommit is the service for code repositories, while CloudWatch handles metrics and monitoring.

options.text: A metrics repository with customizable notification thresholds and channels.

explanation.summary: CloudWatch collects and tracks metrics from AWS resources and custom metrics.
keyPoints: Collects metrics from EC2, RDS, Lambda, and custom sources
Supports alarms and notifications based on thresholds
Integrates with SNS, Lambda, and Auto Scaling
Stores historical metrics for trend analysis
Supports automated actions based on alarms
examples: Monitor CPU utilization of EC2 instances
Receive SNS notifications when RDS storage thresholds exceed limits
explanation.additionalInfo: CloudWatch is a foundational AWS monitoring service that helps maintain operational health and performance visibility.

options.text: A security configuration repository with threat analytics.

explanation.summary: Threat analytics is provided by services like Amazon GuardDuty, not CloudWatch.
explanation.why: CloudWatch focuses on metrics and logging, not security threat analysis.

options.text: A rule repository of a web application firewall with automated vulnerability prevention features.

explanation.summary: WAF rule management is handled by AWS WAF, not CloudWatch.
explanation.why: CloudWatch does not manage web application firewall rules or vulnerability prevention.

questions.question: Which service allows a company with multiple AWS accounts to combine its usage to obtain volume discounts?

explanation.summary: Server Migration Service is for migrating workloads, not billing consolidation.
explanation.why: It does not combine account usage for volume discount purposes.

explanation.summary: AWS Organizations allows consolidation of billing across multiple accounts for volume discounts.
keyPoints: Applies volume pricing and Reserved Instance discounts
examples: Enterprise with multiple AWS accounts combines billing to lower overall charges
Multiple department accounts share consolidated discounts
explanation.additionalInfo: Consolidated billing in AWS Organizations allows enterprises to manage costs efficiently and benefit from aggregated usage discounts.

explanation.summary: AWS Budgets helps monitor and control costs but does not consolidate usage for volume discounts.
explanation.why: It is a budgeting tool, not a billing consolidation service.

explanation.summary: Trusted Advisor provides best-practice recommendations but does not combine account usage for discounts.
explanation.why: It identifies potential cost savings, security risks, and performance improvements, but billing aggregation is handled by Organizations.

questions.question: Which of the following services could be used to deploy an application to servers running on-premises? (Select TWO.)

explanation.summary: Elastic Beanstalk deploys applications in AWS environments, not on on-premises servers.
explanation.why: It automates deployment and scaling in AWS but does not target on-premises infrastructure.

explanation.summary: OpsWorks supports deployment automation using Chef/Puppet for both AWS and on-premises servers.
keyPoints: Can orchestrate stack deployments across environments
examples: Deploy a web application to on-premises Linux servers using OpsWorks
Manage configurations across hybrid environments
explanation.additionalInfo: OpsWorks allows organizations to manage deployments and configuration automation consistently across AWS and on-premises environments.

explanation.summary: CodeDeploy can deploy applications to EC2 instances, on-premises servers, and Lambda functions.
keyPoints: Supports on-premises servers using agent installation
Provides audit and logging for deployments
examples: Deploy updates to a corporate data center server fleet using CodeDeploy
Automate release deployment to hybrid infrastructure
explanation.additionalInfo: CodeDeploy enables reliable deployment across hybrid environments, ensuring consistency and reducing operational overhead.

explanation.summary: AWS Batch runs batch jobs in the cloud, not on on-premises servers.
explanation.why: It is designed for containerized batch workloads on AWS EC2 or Fargate.

explanation.summary: X-Ray is a tracing and monitoring service, not a deployment tool.
explanation.why: It helps analyze and debug distributed applications, but does not deploy software to servers.

questions.question: Which Amazon EC2 pricing model adjusts based on supply and demand of EC2 instances?

explanation.summary: On-Demand instances have fixed hourly pricing and do not fluctuate with supply and demand.
explanation.why: They provide predictable billing without market-based adjustments.

explanation.summary: Reserved Instances provide discounted pricing for a fixed term and do not fluctuate with supply and demand.
explanation.why: RI pricing is committed upfront for 1-3 years, unaffected by spot market dynamics.

explanation.summary: Spot Instances pricing changes based on EC2 spare capacity and market supply/demand.
keyPoints: Use spare capacity at steep discounts
Price fluctuates based on supply and demand
Instances can be interrupted with a two-minute warning
Integrates with Auto Scaling for cost optimization
Supports batch jobs, big data, and CI/CD pipelines
Requires workloads that can tolerate interruptions
examples: Run a compute-intensive batch job on Spot Instances to reduce costs
Scale out analytics pipelines using spot pricing dynamically
explanation.additionalInfo: Spot Instances allow customers to leverage AWS excess capacity at significant savings, with pricing reflecting real-time market conditions.

explanation.summary: Convertible RIs offer flexible instance types within a reservation term but do not fluctuate with supply and demand.
explanation.why: They are reserved for a term with the ability to change instance types, but pricing is fixed for that reservation period.

questions.question: Which design principles for cloud architecture are recommended when re-architecting a large monolithic application? (Select TWO.)

explanation.summary: Manual monitoring is inefficient and not a recommended design principle.
explanation.why: Cloud best practices encourage automated monitoring and observability.

explanation.summary: Fixed servers reduce flexibility and scalability, contrary to cloud principles.
explanation.why: Elasticity and scalability are core cloud design principles; fixed servers hinder dynamic scaling.

explanation.summary: Loose coupling ensures that components can operate independently, enhancing resilience.
examples: Use SQS to decouple application components
Allow microservices to communicate via events instead of direct calls
explanation.additionalInfo: Loose coupling is a core principle when re-architecting monolithic applications into distributed, cloud-native designs.

explanation.summary: Relying on individual components without integration does not ensure scalability or resilience.
explanation.why: Design principles recommend modularity and coordinated communication rather than isolated components.

explanation.summary: Designing for scalability ensures that applications can handle growth in users and workload.
keyPoints: Integrates with Auto Scaling and managed services
Reduces cost by scaling on demand
examples: Scale EC2 instances based on traffic
Use DynamoDB with on-demand capacity for variable workloads
explanation.additionalInfo: Scalability is a fundamental principle in cloud architecture, especially when transforming monolithic systems into microservices or distributed applications.

questions.question: Which is the MINIMUM AWS Support plan that allows for one-hour target response time for support cases?

explanation.summary: Enterprise offers faster response times than Business, but Business is the minimum to meet one-hour SLA for critical cases.
explanation.why: Developer and Basic plans do not offer one-hour response; Enterprise is higher tier but not minimum.

explanation.summary: Business Support plan provides one-hour target response time for urgent (critical) support cases.
keyPoints: Target response time of one hour for urgent issues
Access to AWS Trusted Advisor checks
Includes guidance on AWS best practices
Higher tiers like Enterprise provide additional features like TAM
examples: Production database outage requiring urgent support
Critical EC2 instance failure impacting customer-facing application
explanation.additionalInfo: Business Support is the minimum plan for enterprises needing timely support for production workloads, ensuring one-hour response for critical issues.

explanation.summary: Developer Support offers guidance but does not provide one-hour response for critical issues.
explanation.why: It is intended for non-production workloads and offers slower response targets.

explanation.summary: Basic Support provides only account and billing assistance, no guaranteed response times for technical support.
explanation.why: It is free and intended for learning and account management, not production SLA support.

questions.question: Where can AWS compliance and certification reports be downloaded?

explanation.summary: AWS Artifact provides on-demand access to AWS security and compliance reports.
keyPoints: Includes SOC, ISO, and FedRAMP reports
examples: Download SOC 2 report for audit purposes
Access FedRAMP compliance package for government projects
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Artifact helps customers meet regulatory and compliance obligations by providing authoritative AWS compliance documents on-demand.

explanation.summary: AWS Concierge provides billing and account support, not compliance reports.
explanation.why: It is a support service for enterprise accounts, unrelated to document access.

explanation.summary: Certificate Manager manages SSL/TLS certificates, not compliance reports.
explanation.why: It is for securing web traffic and does not provide compliance documentation.

explanation.summary: Trusted Advisor provides best-practice recommendations, not compliance reports.
explanation.why: It analyzes resources for cost optimization, security, performance, and fault tolerance but does not provide certification reports.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides a customized view of the health of specific AWS services that power a customer’s workloads running on AWS?

explanation.summary: Service Health Dashboard provides general status of AWS services globally, not personalized to a customer.
explanation.why: It displays current status across regions, without customized alerts for individual accounts.

explanation.summary: X-Ray traces requests within applications, not overall AWS service health.
explanation.why: It is focused on application-level tracing and debugging, not service health monitoring.

explanation.summary: Personal Health Dashboard provides account-specific information about AWS service health impacting your resources.
keyPoints: Customized view for a customer’s AWS resources
Provides proactive alerts for service events
Improves incident response and business continuity
examples: Receive notification when EC2 instances in your region may be affected by AWS maintenance
Plan remediation steps based on service degradation alerts
explanation.additionalInfo: Personal Health Dashboard helps customers understand how AWS events affect their specific workloads and provides actionable insights to maintain uptime.

explanation.summary: CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs, not personalized AWS service health.
explanation.why: It collects and analyzes operational data but does not provide account-specific health insights.

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage of consolidated billing on AWS?

explanation.summary: Consolidated billing combines usage across accounts to qualify for volume discounts.
keyPoints: Aggregates usage across multiple accounts in an organization
Enables bulk discounts for compute, storage, and other services
Simplifies billing with a single invoice
Improves cost tracking across departments or projects
examples: Multiple department accounts combine usage to qualify for discounted EC2 pricing
Organization-level consolidated billing reduces overall charges
explanation.additionalInfo: Consolidated billing is a key financial benefit of AWS Organizations, helping enterprises leverage collective usage to reduce costs.

explanation.summary: Consolidated billing does not control access permissions.
explanation.why: IAM and account permissions are separate from billing aggregation.

explanation.summary: Consolidated billing provides a single bill, not multiple bills.
explanation.why: The purpose is to simplify billing by combining accounts, not to generate multiple invoices.

explanation.summary: Tagging is a separate resource management practice and is not eliminated by consolidated billing.
explanation.why: Tags are used for cost allocation, automation, and resource management independent of billing aggregation.

questions.question: Which of the following steps should be taken by a customer when conducting penetration testing on AWS?

options.text: Conduct penetration testing using Amazon Inspector, and then notify AWS support.

explanation.summary: Inspector is a security assessment tool, but AWS requires approval for penetration testing on certain services.
explanation.why: Customers must notify AWS before testing; running immediately violates policy.

options.text: Request and wait for approval from the customer’s internal security team, and then conduct testing.

explanation.summary: Internal approval alone does not fulfill AWS policy requirements.
explanation.why: AWS requires explicit notification/approval before performing penetration tests on AWS infrastructure.

options.text: Notify AWS support, and then conduct testing immediately.

explanation.summary: Notification alone is insufficient; AWS requires request and approval.
explanation.why: Customers must wait for AWS to review and approve penetration testing requests before starting.

options.text: Request and wait for approval from AWS support, and then conduct testing.

explanation.summary: AWS requires customers to submit penetration testing requests and wait for approval before testing certain services.
keyPoints: Submit penetration test request to AWS
Wait for explicit approval before conducting tests
Applies to specific services like EC2, RDS, Lambda, etc.
Helps avoid accidental service disruption or policy violations
Ensures AWS is aware of test activities
Documentation of approval should be retained
examples: Request approval to test EC2 instance firewall configurations
Notify AWS before running network penetration tests on Lambda functions
explanation.additionalInfo: Following the AWS penetration testing policy ensures legal and safe testing practices while protecting AWS infrastructure and other customers.

questions.question: Which of the following AWS features enables a user to launch a pre-configured Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) instance?

explanation.summary: EBS provides block storage, not pre-configured EC2 instances.
explanation.why: While EC2 instances can use EBS volumes, EBS does not define instance configuration templates.

explanation.summary: Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) are pre-configured templates for EC2 instances.
keyPoints: Include operating system, application software, and configuration
Can be customized or use AWS-provided AMIs
Supports versioning and sharing across accounts
Integrates with Auto Scaling and CloudFormation
Used as base images for launch templates
examples: Launch a Linux web server using an AWS-provided AMI
Create a custom AMI with pre-installed software for repeatable deployments
explanation.additionalInfo: AMIs enable consistent, automated provisioning of EC2 instances with the desired software and configuration pre-installed.

explanation.summary: Systems Manager manages and automates operational tasks but does not launch pre-configured instances.
explanation.why: It provides operational control and automation, not instance configuration templates.

explanation.summary: AppStream 2.0 streams applications to users, not launch EC2 instances.
explanation.why: It is a desktop/application streaming service and does not provision EC2 compute resources.

questions.question: How would an AWS customer easily apply common access controls to a large set of users?

options.text: Apply an IAM policy to an IAM group.

explanation.summary: Assigning policies to IAM groups allows multiple users to inherit permissions efficiently.
keyPoints: Groups represent job functions (e.g., admins, developers)
IAM users inherit policies from group membership
Simplifies management of permissions for many users
Changes to the group policy apply to all members
examples: Add new developers to the 'Developers' IAM group to grant S3 access
Modify group policy once to update permissions for all members
explanation.additionalInfo: Using IAM groups is a best practice for managing large user bases, ensuring consistent and auditable permission application.

options.text: Apply an IAM policy to an IAM role.

explanation.summary: Roles are assumed by entities and do not directly manage multiple users' access.
explanation.why: While roles provide temporary credentials for services or users, groups are used to manage multiple users efficiently.

options.text: Apply the same IAM policy to all IAM users with access to the same workload.

explanation.summary: Manually attaching policies to each user is inefficient and error-prone.
explanation.why: IAM groups are recommended to manage permissions collectively rather than individually.

options.text: Apply an IAM policy to an Amazon Cognito user pool.

explanation.summary: Cognito user pools manage authentication for applications, not collective AWS IAM permissions.
explanation.why: They are for app-level user sign-in and identity management, not AWS resource access control.

questions.question: Which AWS Cost Management tool allows you to view the most granular data about your AWS bill?

explanation.summary: Cost Explorer provides visualizations and trends but is less granular than Cost and Usage Reports.
explanation.why: It is for analyzing costs over time rather than detailed line-item billing data.

explanation.summary: AWS Budgets allows you to set cost and usage limits but does not provide granular billing data.
explanation.why: It is for alerts and budget tracking rather than detailed consumption reporting.

explanation.summary: The Cost and Usage Report (CUR) provides the most detailed billing data for AWS usage.
keyPoints: Includes hourly/daily usage and cost data per service
Can be delivered to S3 for analysis
Integrates with Athena, Redshift, QuickSight for querying
Supports cost allocation and reporting needs
examples: Analyze EC2 instance costs per hour across multiple accounts
Generate departmental chargeback reports using CUR data in Athena
explanation.additionalInfo: CUR is the go-to source for detailed AWS billing analysis and supports programmatic querying and integration with analytics tools.

explanation.summary: Billing dashboard provides an overview and summary, not detailed granular usage data.
explanation.why: It is intended for high-level monitoring, not line-item billing analysis.

questions.question: Which of the following can an AWS customer use to launch a new Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) cluster? (Select TWO.)

explanation.summary: AWS Concierge provides billing and support assistance, not cluster provisioning.
explanation.why: It does not launch RDS clusters; the customer must use management tools or APIs.

explanation.summary: CloudFormation templates can define and deploy RDS clusters programmatically.
keyPoints: Declaratively define RDS clusters and associated resources
Automate creation and updates of infrastructure
Allows integration with other AWS services in templates
examples: Deploy a production Aurora cluster with read replicas via CloudFormation
Provision MySQL RDS cluster automatically in multiple regions
explanation.additionalInfo: CloudFormation allows customers to provision RDS clusters as part of infrastructure as code, ensuring consistency and repeatability.

explanation.summary: S3 is object storage and cannot launch RDS clusters.
explanation.why: It stores data but does not manage relational database deployments.

explanation.summary: Auto Scaling manages EC2 instance scaling, not RDS cluster creation.
explanation.why: It scales compute instances but does not provision RDS database clusters.

explanation.summary: The Management Console allows users to launch RDS clusters interactively.
keyPoints: Graphical interface for RDS cluster creation
Step-by-step wizard for engine, instance type, storage
Supports configuration of backups, monitoring, and high availability
Provides visibility into existing clusters and resources
examples: Launch a MySQL RDS cluster through the AWS console
Configure Multi-AZ Aurora cluster interactively
explanation.additionalInfo: The AWS Management Console is a primary method for provisioning and managing RDS clusters, suitable for customers who prefer GUI over code-based deployment.

questions.question: Which of the following is an AWS Cloud architecture design principle?

explanation.summary: Single points of failure should be avoided in cloud architecture.
explanation.why: High availability and fault tolerance require eliminating single points of failure.

explanation.summary: Loose coupling allows components to operate independently, improving scalability and resilience.
examples: Use SQS queues between microservices
Event-driven communication to decouple systems
explanation.additionalInfo: Loose coupling is a core cloud design principle for building resilient, scalable, and maintainable architectures.

explanation.summary: Monolithic design is contrary to cloud-native principles.
explanation.why: Cloud best practices encourage modular, loosely coupled architectures, not monolithic designs.

explanation.summary: Vertical scaling alone is insufficient; cloud design favors elasticity and horizontal scaling.
explanation.why: Over-reliance on vertical scaling creates bottlenecks; horizontal scaling with loose coupling is recommended.

questions.question: Which of the following security measures protect access to an AWS account? (Select TWO.)

explanation.summary: CloudTrail logs activity but does not directly protect access.
explanation.why: It provides auditing and monitoring, not direct access control.

options.text: Grant least privilege access to IAM users.

explanation.summary: Applying least privilege ensures users only have necessary permissions, reducing security risk.
keyPoints: Reduces blast radius if credentials are compromised
Encourages principle of least privilege across IAM users
Can be enforced via IAM policies and groups
examples: Assign only S3 read access to a user who doesn’t need write permissions
Use IAM groups with restricted permissions for developers
explanation.additionalInfo: Least privilege is a core AWS security best practice to minimize risk and ensure proper access control.

options.text: Create one IAM user and share with many developers and users.

explanation.summary: Sharing IAM users is insecure and violates AWS best practices.
explanation.why: Individual IAM users should be created to maintain accountability and control.

explanation.summary: CloudFront is a content delivery network, not an access control measure.
explanation.why: It accelerates content delivery but does not secure account access.

options.text: Activate multi-factor authentication (MFA) for privileged users.

explanation.summary: MFA adds an extra layer of security for AWS accounts, protecting privileged access.
keyPoints: Requires a second factor beyond password
Can be applied to root and IAM users
Supports virtual or hardware MFA devices
Integrates with AWS CLI, SDK, and console
examples: Enable MFA on the root account to prevent unauthorized access
Require MFA for IAM users with administrative privileges
explanation.additionalInfo: MFA is a recommended security measure for protecting AWS accounts, especially for users with high-level permissions.

questions.question: Which service provides a hybrid storage service that enables on-premises applications to seamlessly use cloud storage?

explanation.summary: Glacier is archival storage, not a hybrid storage service.
explanation.why: It is intended for long-term storage and does not integrate on-premises workloads dynamically.

explanation.summary: Snowball is for large-scale data transfer, not continuous hybrid access.
explanation.why: It physically moves data into AWS, but does not provide live hybrid storage capabilities.

explanation.summary: Storage Gateway enables on-premises applications to seamlessly access AWS cloud storage.
keyPoints: Provides hybrid cloud storage for file, volume, and tape
Low-latency access to cloud storage from on-premises
Supports backup, archiving, and disaster recovery
Integrates with AWS services like S3 and Glacier
Simplifies cloud adoption for legacy applications
Supports caching for frequently accessed data
examples: Use Storage Gateway to extend on-premises file shares to S3
Migrate backup tapes to cloud while keeping local access
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Storage Gateway allows organizations to integrate existing on-premises applications with AWS cloud storage seamlessly, providing a bridge for hybrid cloud adoption.

explanation.summary: EBS is block storage for EC2 instances, not a hybrid storage solution.
explanation.why: It does not provide on-premises integration for existing applications.

questions.question: Which of the following services falls under the responsibility of the customer to maintain operating system configuration, security patching, and networking?

explanation.summary: RDS is a managed database service; AWS handles OS and patching.
explanation.why: Customers manage the database schema and data, but the underlying OS is maintained by AWS.

explanation.summary: Customers are responsible for OS configuration, patching, and networking on EC2 instances.
examples: Patch a Linux EC2 instance regularly to prevent vulnerabilities
Configure security groups and network ACLs for EC2 instances
explanation.additionalInfo: EC2 is an Infrastructure-as-a-Service offering, where the customer manages the OS, applications, and networking while AWS provides the underlying hardware.

explanation.summary: ElastiCache is managed; AWS handles OS patching and infrastructure.
explanation.why: Customers manage the data structure and access patterns but not OS or network settings.

explanation.summary: Fargate abstracts the OS layer; AWS manages OS and networking.
explanation.why: Customers only define container tasks and resource requirements; AWS handles the underlying infrastructure.

questions.question: Which of the following is an important architectural design principle when designing cloud applications?

explanation.summary: Deploying across multiple Availability Zones improves fault tolerance and availability.
keyPoints: Reduces impact of failures in a single AZ
Supports high availability and disaster recovery
Integrates with Auto Scaling and ELB
examples: Deploy web servers in two AZs to maintain uptime
Replicate RDS databases across multiple AZs
explanation.additionalInfo: Multiple AZ deployments are a fundamental AWS best practice for designing resilient, highly available cloud applications.

explanation.summary: Tightly coupled components reduce fault tolerance and scalability.
explanation.why: Loose coupling is recommended to improve resilience and maintainability.

explanation.summary: Open source usage is optional and not a core architectural principle.
explanation.why: AWS best practices focus on availability, scalability, and security rather than licensing model.

explanation.summary: Provisioning extra capacity statically is less efficient than leveraging elasticity.
explanation.why: Cloud design principles encourage dynamic scaling to optimize costs and performance.

questions.question: Which AWS support plan includes a dedicated Technical Account Manager?

explanation.summary: Developer Support does not include a dedicated TAM.
explanation.why: It is intended for non-production workloads and offers guidance only via general support channels.

explanation.summary: Enterprise Support includes a dedicated Technical Account Manager (TAM).
keyPoints: Provides a single point of contact for critical issues
Includes access to AWS Trusted Advisor checks
examples: Enterprise customer receives TAM support during a major migration
Dedicated TAM coordinates with AWS teams for compliance requirements
explanation.additionalInfo: The Enterprise plan is designed for large organizations with critical workloads needing expert guidance and direct AWS engagement.

explanation.summary: Business Support provides faster response times but no dedicated TAM.
explanation.why: It is aimed at production workloads but does not include a personal Technical Account Manager.

explanation.summary: Basic Support provides only account and billing assistance, no TAM.
explanation.why: It is free and intended for learning and account management, not enterprise-level support.

questions.question: Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) offers which of the following benefits over traditional database management?

options.text: AWS manages the data stored in Amazon RDS tables.

explanation.summary: Customers manage the data; AWS manages infrastructure, backups, and maintenance.
explanation.why: RDS automates operational tasks, but the customer owns the actual database content.

options.text: AWS manages the maintenance of the operating system.

explanation.summary: RDS is a managed service where AWS handles OS and database software maintenance.
keyPoints: Focus on application logic rather than OS management
examples: RDS automatically applies critical security patches
AWS maintains the OS for an Aurora DB instance
explanation.additionalInfo: RDS abstracts the underlying infrastructure, letting customers focus on data and applications while AWS manages OS, patching, and failover.

options.text: AWS automatically scales up instance types on demand.

explanation.summary: RDS does not automatically change instance types without customer intervention.
explanation.why: Scaling requires manual modification or use of Aurora Auto Scaling for read replicas; not all engines auto-scale compute.

explanation.summary: Customers choose the database engine and type.
explanation.why: AWS provides supported engines, but the customer selects the engine and version for their workload.

questions.question: Amazon ElastiCache is best for storing common database query results, which helps to alleviate database access load.

explanation.summary: Amazon Machine Learning is for predictive analytics, not caching query results.
explanation.why: It analyzes data but does not store query results to reduce database load.

explanation.summary: SQS is a messaging service and does not cache database queries.
explanation.why: It decouples application components via message queues but does not alleviate database access through caching.

explanation.summary: ElastiCache is a managed in-memory caching service that reduces database load by storing frequently accessed data.
keyPoints: Improves throughput and reduces database query load
Facilitates session management, leaderboard, and caching scenarios
examples: Cache the results of frequent SQL queries to reduce load on RDS
Store session data for a web application in ElastiCache
explanation.additionalInfo: ElastiCache improves application performance and scalability by offloading repeated database queries and storing hot data in-memory.

explanation.summary: EC2 Instance Store provides ephemeral block storage for instances, not a caching layer for databases.
explanation.why: It is local to the instance and does not provide shared caching capabilities.

questions.question: Which of the following is a component of the shared responsibility model managed entirely by AWS?

explanation.summary: OS patching for customer-managed EC2 instances is the customer’s responsibility.
explanation.why: AWS manages OS patching only for managed services like RDS, not for user-managed instances.

explanation.summary: Customers manage encryption of data at rest and in transit for their workloads.
explanation.why: AWS provides the tools, but the implementation is customer responsibility.

explanation.summary: MFA configuration is a customer responsibility.
explanation.why: Customers enable and manage MFA for IAM users and root accounts.

explanation.summary: AWS is responsible for the security and auditing of the underlying data center infrastructure.
keyPoints: Includes data center audits and inspections
Foundation of AWS security of the cloud
examples: AWS audits its data centers for SOC and ISO compliance
Ensures physical access logs and surveillance are maintained
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS manages the security of the cloud infrastructure, including physical assets, while customers manage security in the cloud.

questions.question: Which options does AWS make available for customers who want to learn about security in the cloud in an instructor-led setting? (Select TWO.)

explanation.summary: Trusted Advisor is a tool for best-practice checks, not instructor-led training.
explanation.why: It provides automated guidance but does not offer classroom instruction.

explanation.summary: AWS Online Tech Talks provide instructor-led or live virtual sessions for learning AWS security practices.
keyPoints: Covers security, compliance, and best practices
Updates content regularly with latest AWS features
examples: Attend a live session on AWS security best practices
Join a Tech Talk about identity and access management
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Online Tech Talks provide a virtual classroom experience to help customers learn security practices and other AWS topics.

explanation.summary: AWS Blog provides articles but is not instructor-led.
explanation.why: It offers guidance and announcements but not interactive classroom sessions.

explanation.summary: Forums are community Q&A platforms, not instructor-led training.
explanation.why: They allow peer discussion but do not provide structured classroom learning.

explanation.summary: AWS Classroom Training provides in-person or live instructor-led sessions on cloud security and other topics.
keyPoints: Covers AWS security, compliance, and operational best practices
Can be private on-site or public classes
examples: Attend an on-site AWS Security Essentials class
Participate in a live lab on configuring IAM and MFA
explanation.additionalInfo: Classroom Training is ideal for customers seeking guided, instructor-led AWS learning experiences with practical exercises and expert feedback.

questions.question: Which of the following features can be configured through the Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) Dashboard? (Select TWO.)

explanation.summary: CloudFront distributions are managed through the CloudFront console, not the VPC dashboard.
explanation.why: VPC focuses on networking resources, not content delivery networks.

explanation.summary: Route 53 is a DNS service and is not configured through the VPC dashboard.
explanation.why: DNS zones and records are managed separately from VPC networking.

explanation.summary: Security groups are a core VPC networking feature used to control traffic to instances.
keyPoints: Acts as a virtual firewall for EC2 instances
Rules can be configured for inbound and outbound traffic
Can be reused across multiple instances
Changes apply immediately to associated resources
Essential for network-level security within VPC
examples: Allow HTTP traffic on port 80 to web servers
Restrict SSH access to a specific IP range
explanation.additionalInfo: Security Groups are fundamental for isolating and controlling access to instances in a VPC environment.

explanation.summary: Subnets are VPC features that divide the network into smaller segments.
keyPoints: Control routing and access to resources
Used for organizing and securing resources
Allows IP range allocation within VPC
Integrates with security groups and NACLs
examples: Create a public subnet for web servers and a private subnet for databases
Assign different routing tables to subnets for internet access control
explanation.additionalInfo: Subnets are foundational for organizing and securing AWS network resources and controlling access within VPCs.

explanation.summary: ELB is managed outside the VPC dashboard, though it connects to VPC resources.
explanation.why: ELB is configured via the EC2 or ELB console and integrates with VPC networks but is not directly configured through VPC settings.

questions.question: If each department within a company has its own AWS account, what is one way to enable consolidated billing?

options.text: Use AWS Budgets on each account to pay only to budget.

explanation.summary: Budgets are for monitoring and alerts, not consolidating accounts.
explanation.why: AWS Budgets cannot aggregate multiple accounts for combined billing or volume discounts.

options.text: Contact AWS Support for a monthly bill.

explanation.summary: AWS Support cannot consolidate billing manually on request.
explanation.why: Consolidated billing is handled through AWS Organizations, not support tickets.

options.text: Create an AWS Organization from the payer account and invite the other accounts to join.

explanation.summary: AWS Organizations allows consolidated billing by linking multiple accounts under a master account.
